title: Five records per three-year bin left no North American cells in a 1960-1974 to 2000-2014 bumblebee comparison
abstract: We tested time coverage in a public bumblebee climate-impact archive. Cells needed enough records for equal total draws in both periods. Requiring five records in every three-year bin then reduced eligible cells from 183 to two in Europe and from 72 to zero in North America for 1960-1974 to 2000-2014. For 1975-1986 to 1988-1999, counts fell from 135 to 50 and from 37 to eight. Exact expected richness changes under pooled and fixed-bin draws had the same mean sign in the three available samples. All three paired allocation intervals included zero, with only two to nine spatial blocks. The sparse later sample cannot support a regional comparison. Equal record totals do not ensure balanced time coverage. The test does not estimate a climate effect, true richness change or air pollution effects. Selection of well-recorded cells, source overlap and unknown detection limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure support reproduction. External records and cell tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Cells with enough total records in both periods versus cells with at least five records in each three-year bin. Cell counts are exact for the selected archive and rules. Panels have separate vertical scales. Zero later North American support prevents a draw-design comparison.
